metadata.goal: Examine the operating conditions of the given vessels passing through the corridor on two days and compare them.
metadata.dataset_description: The main table contains timestamped vessel positions and AIS-style movement attributes. The vessel table contains stable vessel attributes shared across trajectory segments.

insight_list.insight: The first day has three times as many vessels passing clearly through the corridor as the second day.

plot.title: Two-hour corridor entries by day
plot.description: The plot provides the visual comparison needed for this question.

insight_list.question: How does the number of vessels passing through the corridor differ between the two days?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the two-hour profile of distinct corridor entries, rather than using only the daily total.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df[d['sog']>=5].copy(); d['timestamp']=pd.to_datetime(d['timestamp']); first=d.groupby(['day','trajectory_id'])['timestamp'].min().reset_index(); first['two_hour_window']=(first.timestamp.dt.hour//2)*2; profile=first.groupby(['day','two_hour_window']).size().unstack(0,fill_value=0); profile.plot(marker='o'); plt.ylabel('distinct corridor entries'); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: On the first day, nearly all corridor passages are eastbound along the mapped east-west corridor, whereas the second day contains a much more balanced mix of eastbound and westbound passages.

plot.title: Through-corridor direction by day
plot.description: The plot provides the visual comparison needed for this question.

insight_list.question: Do vessels use the corridor in the same direction on both days?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Infer direction from ordered trajectory endpoints and interpret it relative to the mapped corridor orientation.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
d=df.copy(); d=d[d['sog']>=5]; g=d.groupby(['day','trajectory_id']); direction=g['lon'].agg(['first','last']); direction['direction']=direction.apply(lambda r:'eastbound' if r['last']>=r['first'] else 'westbound',axis=1); print(direction.groupby(['day','direction']).size())

insight_list.insight: The second day has more than twice as many vessels anchored near the corridor as the first day.

plot.title: Anchored vessels by day and ship type
plot.description: The plot provides the visual comparison needed for this question.

insight_list.question: How does anchoring near the corridor differ between the two days?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare day totals while retaining the ship-type segments that make up each total.

insight_list.insight: On both days, anchored vessels are predominantly classified as Cargo, with only a small number assigned to other ship-type categories.

plot.description: The plot provides the visual comparison needed for this question.

insight_list.question: Which ship types dominate the anchored vessels on each day?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare ship-type composition within the anchored subset separately by day and retain small non-cargo categories.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
d=df[df['nav_status'].eq('At anchor')].drop_duplicates('trajectory_id'); print(pd.crosstab(d['day'], d['ship_type']))

insight_list.insight: Only a small number of vessels pass through the corridor on both days, while four vessels—about half of the first day's anchored vessels—are anchored near the corridor on both days.

plot.title: Cross-day vessel recurrence
plot.description: The plot provides the visual comparison needed for this question.

insight_list.question: Which vessels recur across the two days, and do they repeat passage or anchoring behavior?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Match vessels by their stable vessel identifier before comparing their day-specific movement state.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
d=df.copy(); days=d.groupby('vessel_id')['day'].nunique(); repeated=days[days==2].index; a=d[d['vessel_id'].isin(repeated)]; print(a.groupby(['vessel_id','day'])['nav_status'].first())

insights: The first day has three times as many vessels passing clearly through the corridor as the second day.
On the first day, nearly all corridor passages are eastbound along the mapped east-west corridor, whereas the second day contains a much more balanced mix of eastbound and westbound passages.
The second day has more than twice as many vessels anchored near the corridor as the first day.
On both days, anchored vessels are predominantly classified as Cargo, with only a small number assigned to other ship-type categories.
Only a small number of vessels pass through the corridor on both days, while four vessels—about half of the first day's anchored vessels—are anchored near the corridor on both days.
summary: The two-day case contrasts a busy, predominantly eastbound passage day with a quieter, directionally balanced day that has substantially more anchoring near the corridor and limited vessel recurrence.
